brief: US stocks trade higher on 3 September 2026 on three inputs. Fed Governor Waller said recent data suggest signs of disinflation and that if the next two weeks confirm it he would support holding the funds rate. That eased bond investor concerns ahead of the meeting in two weeks and 10-year yields fell 3bp to 4.75%, which supports equities. Waller frames inflation as a rate of change, so although gasoline and tariffs remain well above two years ago, lapping the tariff peak and a possible month-over-month gasoline peak may mean that pressure is already dissipating. Second, ISM Services rose 1.3 points to 55.4 on strong new orders, against an ISM Manufacturing decline earlier in the week, and services sentiment improved in China, India and Brazil. Goldman reads services as more nimble than manufacturing, while noting post-pandemic sentiment has tracked activity less closely. Q2 productivity was unrevised at +1.4% annualized and +2.2% year over year, and the GDP tracker was cut 20bp to 2.5% (body says 2Q, cited title says Q3). Third, SNOW rose over 20% on revenue and margin beats while AVGO fell over 5% on fiscal 4Q guidance below the Street. Goldman stays Buy. Payrolls Friday, Goldman forecasts 40k.
